edges.effect_quant: A 2024 three-arm randomized trial in 200 adults with IBS-D found that heat-treated Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 reduced IBS Symptom Severity Scale scores far more than placebo over 12 weeks, with mean Day-84 change around -178 points versus -60 with placebo. Smaller postbiotic trials in IBS have generally moved barrier or symptom endpoints in the same favorable direction, but the evidence base is still product-specific rather than class-wide.
edges.population: adults with irritable bowel syndrome, especially diarrhea-predominant or mixed-type disease, receiving heat-treated or fermentation-derived postbiotic interventions
edges.mechanism: Postbiotics may improve global IBS symptom scores by calming mucosal immune activation and strengthening barrier integrity without relying on live-organism colonization. The best current IBS data point toward reduced mast-cell activity, improved epithelial resistance, and downstream reductions in pain, stool instability, and symptom burden.
edges.summary: Postbiotics look promising for reducing overall IBS symptom burden, but the evidence is still early and product-specific. The strongest recent trial showed a large improvement in IBS severity scores with a heat-treated Bifidobacterium product in IBS-D, while smaller studies using other postbiotic preparations support barrier or symptom improvement rather than giving a settled class effect.
edges.caveats: This is not yet a mature, interchangeable category: different postbiotics use different organisms, fermentation products, and delivery routes, and some supporting studies focus on mechanistic or open-label outcomes rather than hard replicated clinical endpoints. The fair reading is encouraging but still not plug-and-play across all postbiotic products.

evidence.notes: A randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of live Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 (ES1) and heat-treated Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 (HT-ES1) in participants with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome.
